raw.rationale: The presence of recurrent, intermittent, painless hematuria with 70% dysmorphic red cells on phase-contrast microscopy is highly suggestive of a glomerular origin, and IgA nephropathy is a common cause of this presentation.

rejected.label: Nephrolithiasis
rejected.why: Although the patient has small stones in the left kidney, the presence of dysmorphic red cells suggests a glomerular rather than a urological cause of hematuria.

rejected.label: Thin basement membrane nephropathy
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with isolated hematuria, but the presence of systemic hypertension and the use of herbal remedies may suggest a more complex diagnosis.

rejected.label: Alport syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is typically associated with sensorineural hearing loss and eye abnormalities, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Medullary sponge kidney
rejected.why: This condition is a cause of nephrolithiasis, but it does not typically present with dysmorphic red cells on urinalysis.
